key_insight: Combining histopathology AI, predicted morphological features, and manually assessed PRAME staining achieved similar malignancy discrimination to the standalone AI classifier.
clinical_relevance: The framework offers a structured way to combine AI outputs with established pathology findings, but improved diagnostic performance or patient outcomes was not demonstrated.
method: Analyzed H&E whole-slide images using the Virchow2 foundation model and STAMP framework.
Trained models to classify malignancy and predict established morphological features.
Integrated AI scores and predicted features with manually assessed PRAME immunohistochemistry.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective cohort of 1,000 lesions, models trained on 800 cases achieved test AUROCs of 0.970 for standalone AI and 0.972 for the integrated model on 200 temporally held-out cases.
watch_item: Evaluation was limited to a retrospective cohort selected for PRAME testing; broader generalizability and prospective clinical utility remain unestablished.
paper_title: Integrating Histopathology Foundation Models and PRAME Immunohistochemistry in Melanoma Diagnosis
